items.title: OpenAI will honor shared robots.txt signals for sites to express AI training preferences
items.summary: OpenAI has announced that it will comply with a shared robots.txt signal, allowing website operators to express their training preferences to participating AI providers. This mechanism is designed to simplify communication of preferences between websites and AI providers.
items.comment: This could become another industry signal for sites to express training preferences, but the actual binding will still depend on the scope of participating providers.

items.title: OpenAI publishes community safety report and strengthens protection for youth
items.summary: OpenAI releases a community safety report and announces enhancements to ChatGPT’s violence prevention, including expanded protection measures, early intervention, and a commitment to public security reporting.
items.comment: It is worth noting that platforms are incorporating youth protection and violence prevention into more public safety reporting mechanisms.

items.title: OpenAI updates Model Spec and proposes five core values
items.summary: OpenAI releases an updated Model Spec, proposing five core values to guide more powerful AI’s judgment, human agency, and fidelity to human intent.
items.comment: This may affect ChatGPT's behavioral boundaries in value conflict scenarios.

items.title: OpenAI issued a document advocating fair use to support AI training and innovation
items.summary: OpenAI published an article sharing excerpts from court opinions submitted by creators, academics, accessibility advocates, and legal experts, advocating fair use to support AI training and innovation.
items.comment: It is worth noting that training data copyright disputes are advancing simultaneously on two fronts: litigation and legislation.

items.title: Australia's AI copyright reform criticized as potentially unconstitutional and triggering huge compensation
items.summary: Australian Coalition senators and the recording industry have warned that changing copyright laws to allow AI companies to scrape music, books and news could pose constitutional issues and trigger huge "just clauses" compensation from rights holders around the world. Constitutional law expert Anne Twomey said depending on how the legislation is drafted, this "could" amount to a government taking property.
items.comment: This may increase legislative uncertainty in Australia regarding the licensing of AI training data.

items.title: US defense contractor accused of connecting personal Claude Code account to Pentagon systems
items.summary: An Accenture contractor earlier this year connected a secure centralized system used by multiple intelligence agencies to his personal Claude Code account, WIRED reported, citing sources. The AI agent then sent system information containing login credentials to high-risk third-party websites; the agent was operating on the DOD network for two months before it was discovered. Accenture said the allegations were determined to be without merit after a thorough independent investigation.
items.comment: Of concern are the enterprise deployment boundaries and credential management risks of agent-based coding tools.

items.title: Claude Code's VS Code extension has backdoor discovered in Cursor Marketplace
items.summary: Phorion said it discovered a persistent SSH backdoor in the official Claude Code for VS Code extensions 2.1.312 and 2.1.313 distributed on the Cursor Marketplace, and Cursor has removed the affected versions. Phorion's update says the Cursor security advisory lists macOS and Windows versions as affected.
items.comment: It is worth noting that supply chain security expanded by AI coding is becoming a new attack surface.

items.title: AI ghost hunting app has been downloaded over one million times, and the community has tightened AI content policies at the same time
items.summary: The Guardian reports that GhostTube Seer is available as a paid subscription and Google Play shows more than 1 million downloads; the app maps phone sensor signals into words and uses an image generator to generate images. Reports also claim that communities such as r/Nosleep have strict policies banning AI-generated content.
items.comment: This may reflect that generative AI is changing the content production and trust mechanisms of niche interest communities.

items.title: DoorDash says third-party AI agents only brought in "hundreds" of orders
items.summary: DoorDash said on its third-quarter earnings call that orders from third-party agents such as Muse, Instinct, Fo and others were only in the "hundreds" and the company reported an average of 3 million daily deliveries in 2025. CEO Tony Xu said it still wants to understand agent use cases and work with agent developers.
items.comment: This may indicate that the actual penetration of agency commerce is still in its early stages.

items.title: Google admits AI search revenue per query is lower than traditional search, expands advertising
items.summary: Alphabet admitted on its third-quarter earnings call that AI Mode brings in less revenue per query than traditional web searches, in part because of fewer ads; the company plans to expand AI Mode advertising in more international markets and introduce multiple rounds of advertising in the United States. The stock price fell sharply after the earnings report was released.
items.comment: It is worth noting that the commercialization efficiency of AI search may continue to affect the search advertising model.

items.title: Amazon Q3: AWS grows 39.3%, AI capital expenditures in 2026 will be approximately $220 billion
items.summary: Amazon’s third-quarter financial report showed that AWS sales increased by 39.3% year-on-year, the fastest growth rate in the past five years; CEO Andy Jassy said that cash capital expenditures in 2026 will be approximately US$220 billion, mostly for AWS, and is expected to increase significantly in 2027. Jassy also said AWS has an annualized revenue run rate of $184 billion and can become a trillion-dollar revenue business in the next five to ten years.
items.comment: It is worth paying attention to the payback period between AI infrastructure spending and cloud business growth.

items.title: Reddit moves to a logged-in user-focused experience to cope with AI search and crawling
items.summary: Reddit announced during its third-quarter earnings call that it would move to a primarily logged-in user experience to protect data from AI scraping and advance model provider licensing transactions; the company said search recommendations dropped by more than 1 million times per week on average in October. In the third quarter, global daily activity was 130.3 million, which was the same as the previous quarter. Daily activity in the United States dropped from 53.2 million to 50.7 million.
items.comment: This could exacerbate tensions between open web content and AI training and licensing.

items.title: Thrive Holdings acquires ADT for $15.3 billion enterprise value, plans to transform home security with AI
items.summary: Thrive Holdings announced the acquisition of ADT for $10 per share, or approximately $7.6 billion in equity, with a transaction enterprise value of $15.3 billion; Thrive Holdings partnered with OpenAI and received investment from OpenAI, planning to transform the home security business with AI.
items.comment: It is worth noting that transactions involving AI transforming traditional industries are proceeding in the form of mergers and acquisitions.

items.title: Rivian licenses AI voice assistant technology to Volkswagen joint venture
items.summary: Rivian said in third-quarter investor materials that it would partially license its AI voice assistant technology to Volkswagen Group, expanding the $5.8 billion joint venture between the two parties; it did not disclose licensing fees, payment terms or specific models. Reports indicate that the assistant may first be used in Volkswagen's low-cost electric car ID EVERY1.
items.comment: This may become a case where car companies use AI assistants as software licensing assets.

items.title: Runware plans to mass-produce prefabricated AI data centers like cars
items.summary: Runware told TechCrunch that it plans to mass-produce prefabricated AI data centers on an assembly line basis at its Romanian factory, reaching a production capacity of 30 megawatts per day, or about 1 gigawatt per month, by 2028, and aims to complete on-site go-live within 48 hours. The company said it already has one factory that has been in use for several years and is building a second; the scale is still planned.
items.comment: It is worth watching whether prefabricated modularity can solve the delivery bottleneck of AI data centers.

items.title: Survey: 55% of lawyers in Victoria use AI, only 26% reduce client fees
items.summary: A Victorian Legal Services Commission survey of 2221 lawyers showed 55 per cent were using AI in their work, up from 37 per cent last year; 79 per cent were using consumer chatbots such as ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini or Copilot. Only 26% said AI resulted in lower customer fees, and 46% said customers came in with inaccurate information.
items.comment: This may indicate that efficiency improvements have not yet translated simultaneously into lower prices for customers.

items.title: US university administrator gets religious exemption from using AI in work
items.summary: TechCrunch reports that University of Kentucky administrator and non-theistic humanist David Durman has received a religious exemption from using AI in the workplace, and the American Humanist Association says he is the first humanist to receive such an accommodation. The school said it reviews religious accommodation requests on a case-by-case basis.
items.comment: This could provide an early example of religious or belief-facilitated controversies surrounding the use of AI in the workplace.

items.title: Investor’s Last Exam: Financial intelligence is good at research but weak at prediction
items.summary: The paper proposes the Investor’s Last Exam stock research benchmark, which contains 3.43 million document versions and 86 tasks, and uses expert standards to simultaneously evaluate research quality, forecast accuracy and simulated investment performance. The abstract states that GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus lead with 5.5 overall scores (68.1 and 66.9), but Astra only scored 52.5 in Forecast & Model, showing that top models still have difficulty converting research capabilities into predictive capabilities.
items.comment: It is worth noting that the benchmark advances the focus of assessment from knowledge questions and answers to the evidence-hypothesis-judgment chain.

items.title: Technical practice: FurtherAI claims that the AI native engineering process brings about 5 times the amount of code changes
items.summary: The author of FurtherAI stated that the number of code changes merged per engineer per day has increased by about 5 times since January, and the rollback rate is less than 0.5%; agents write code and tests, and AI reviews 99% of changes before humans, and up to one-third of changes can be merged without human participation. The authors also say the team used 21 automated rules to translate engineering experience into commit checks.
items.comment: The authors' experience may be difficult to directly extrapolate to higher risk systems.

items.title: Technical practice: Simon Willison looks at using cutting-edge model agents to independently develop multiplayer games
items.summary: Simon Willison introduced Jacob Sansbury's Spawn: a multiplayer game environment where players can use prompts to let the in-game agent Savi modify the world; Jacob said that its development is independently promoted by a group of Fable-driven agents, with a monthly token cost of more than $3 million and online changes every hour. Willison was surprised by how well the pattern worked in games, but said it was hard to imagine it being used in riskier software.
items.comment: Such experiments may provide edge cases for agent-based development, but the costs and risks remain to be seen.
